newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says EMU timetable remains unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Germany says EMU timetable remains unchanged.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry, amid market rumours of an impending announcement of a delay in the introduction of Europe's single currency, said on Friday the timetable for European economic and monetary union (EMU) was unchanged.
"The timetable remains," a ministry spokesman told reporters in Bonn.
The statement follows earlier denials by the finance ministry and the Bundesbank of plans for any statement from Germany that would suggest a delay in the start of EMU.

Talk that the launch of the single currency -- scheduled for 1999 -- could be delayed apparently originated in markets in London, but spread like wildfire with traders seeing a delay as a possibility, while conceding that it would not be likely that such a major announcement would be made out of the blue.

Problems faced by almost all European states in reining in their budget deficits to bring them under the threshold laid down in the Mastricht Treaty has led many economists to increase the probability rating of a delay in the start.
Countries which want to enter EMU in 1999 must meet set targets on inflation, exchange rates, interest rates, deficits and public debt.
The Bonn finance ministry pointed out again that a decision on EMU participants would not be made until 1998 and that any speculation now was superfluous.
